title: Marinid Sultanate
capsule: The Marinids were a Zenata Berber dynasty that displaced the Almohad Caliphate, capturing Fez in 1248 and Marrakesh in 1269 to unite Morocco. Under Abu Yusuf Yaqub (r.1258–1286) and his successors they mounted repeated interventions in Iberia alongside the Nasrid Kingdom of Granada, briefly holding Algeciras and Ceuta in contests with Castile, and patronized the great madrasa-building program in Fez that produced the Bou Inania and Attarine colleges. Marinid power declined sharply after the Black Death (1348) devastated their population base; the dynasty lost effective control of Fez to the Wattasid viziers c.1420 and was extinguished when the last nominal Marinid sultan was killed in 1465.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Marinid core territory in Morocco is well attested from Arabic chronicles and Portuguese coastal surveys; Iberian holdings were ephemeral and boundaries are approximate; the dataset's 1250–1467 span aligns well with the documentary record.
